amendments.reason: Messaging owns the identity of one SendToContact intent: a caller requestId bound, permanently, to the sha256 of its semantic payload, so the same requestId with a changed payload is an idempotency conflict even after a refusal that created no Message. One row per requestId with exactly that hash and its creation time; it stores no message, outcome, route, conversation, Contact, provider identifier or transport, and the one Message the intent may admit is found by its derived clientMessageId "stc:" + requestId. It is written by exactly one Messaging adapter, insert-if-absent and read only, with no update or delete path. It is pending source state created by an expand-only migration and is intentionally not asserted as deployed production inventory.
